issues.legal_issue: The legislative competence to impose a tax on forest-land excavation and non-forest use when the levy is not imposed on land as a unit.
material_facts: A state enactment imposed charges in connection with excavation of forest land and its use for non-forest purposes.
For excavation, the charge was calculated by reference to the area of land voided or subsided; charges for non-forest use varied with the land’s vegetative density and period of use.
The enactment made users or occupiers liable, including persons who might not own the land.
The enactment did not impose a charge where the land had been rehabilitated or restored.
Existing central law contained provisions for reclamation and rehabilitation of forest land, including planting and re-planting trees.
issues.conclusion: The levy was, in substance, on excavation and non-forest use, or on the absence of land, rather than a tax directly imposed on land as a unit. It therefore did not fall within Entry 49 of List II, and the state legislature lacked competence to enact the law. The provisions concerning use of forest land for non-forest purposes also impinged on the central forest-conservation regime. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Entry 49 of List II permits a tax directly imposed on land or buildings as units and bearing a direct relationship to them; it does not permit a tax on an activity merely because that activity occurs on land, or a tax on the absence of land created by excavation. The Court applied Sudhir Chandra Nawn v. Wealth Tax Officer, Calcutta, [1961] 1 SCR 108; Second Gift Tax Officer, Mangalore v. D.H. Nazareth, [1971] 1 SCR 195; India Cement Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu, [1990] 1 SCC 12; Union of India v. H.S. Dhillon, [1972] 2 SCR 33; Orissa Cement Ltd. v. State of Orissa, [1991] Supp. 1 SCC 430; and State of Orissa v. Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd., [1995] Supp. 2 SCC 686. It distinguished Goodriche Group Ltd. v. State of West Bengal, [1995] Supp. 1 SCC 707, where the tax was imposed on existing land and the produce was only a measure of the tax. The Court also held that the provisions concerning reclamation and rehabilitation of forest land fell within the field covered by the Forest Conservation Act, 1980. The relevant constitutional provision was Entry 49 of List II; the Court noted the relevance of Entry 54 of List I and the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957.

rule.if: challenge_to_state_tax_law and levy_attaches_after_excavation_or_nonforest_use and (amount_tracks_extent_of_void_or_use or no_levy_after_reclamation) and payer_is_user_or_occupier

predicates.challenge_to_state_tax_law: A proceeding challenged a state enactment that imposed a tax.
predicates.levy_attaches_after_excavation_or_nonfor: The state imposed the levy when a person excavated land or used it for a non-forest purpose.
predicates.amount_tracks_extent_of_void_or_use: The amount of the levy varied according to the area excavated, left void, or used for a non-forest purpose.
predicates.no_levy_after_reclamation: The levy was not imposed if the land had been rehabilitated or restored.
predicates.payer_is_user_or_occupier: The enactment made the person using or occupying the land liable, whether or not that person owned it.

issues.definition: When a challenged state tax attaches to excavation or non-forest use, is measured by the resulting void or use or ceases after reclamation, and is payable by a user or occupier, the rule treats the law as invalid for lack of state legislative competence.
